research.topic: Largest country without a permanent river: Saudi Arabia, about 2.15 million km², has no perennial rivers and no natural lakes; rainfall is rare and runs briefly through wadis (dry valleys). It is the world's largest producer of desalinated water (about a fifth of global output, SWCC), supplying more than half of its drinking water. The Jubail–Riyadh transmission system carries desalinated water from the Gulf coast to Riyadh, roughly 460–480 km inland and about 600–700 m uphill. Australia has permanent rivers (Murray–Darling) alongside many ephemeral ones; Egypt's population lives along the Nile.

myths.myth: Every big country has at least one river.
myths.reality: Saudi Arabia, larger than Western Europe, has no river that flows all year and no natural lake; its wadis run only for days after rain.
